source.title: Universal Neurons in GPT2 Language Models
source.authors: Wes Gurnee; T. Horsley; Zifan Carl Guo; Tara Rezaei Kheirkhah; Qinyi Sun; W. Hathaway; Neel Nanda; Dimitris Bertsimas

record.tranche_reason: The study measures neuron-level recurrence across random seeds and finds it is limited to a small fraction of neurons, refining claims of broad universality. It does not test convergence of whole-model representations or cross-modal alignment.
record.gate_note: The study reports neuron activation correlations across seeds, compared with a random-rotation baseline, and counts neurons above an excess-correlation threshold. Those results are included below. The threshold of excess correlation greater than 0.5 is a criterion used to identify universal neurons, not a separate outcome. The study also reports qualitative interpretations and neuron families, which are not separately rowed as they do not give distinct recurrence outcomes beyond the measured universality results.
record.test_reason: The study adapts the unit-matching method of the original Convergent Learning source to GPT2 and Pythia replicas trained from different seeds. It computes maximum pairwise activation correlations between neurons, against a random-rotation baseline. Its results bear directly on V3 (convergence across seeds at the unit level) and on V5 (recurrence of interpretable neurons). The study does not measure whole-representation alignment, scale trends in that alignment, cross-modal pairs or mappings.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that only about 1-5% of neurons are universal across seeds, and take this as evidence that individual neurons are not the right unit of analysis. The few universal neurons are often interpretable, fall into a few families, and some have clear functional roles (entropy modulation, attention deactivation, token prediction and suppression). The authors note the scope is narrow: small models, with neuron universality across seeds within the same family.
record.recipe_differences: Measures individual-neuron activation correlations across seed replicas and subtracts a random-rotation baseline; it does not compare whole-model representation distances or use the original study's representation-level method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported prevalence varies by model: GPT2-small is higher than GPT2-medium and Pythia-160M. Universality also depends on the chosen excess-correlation threshold, which the authors say has no principled cutoff.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT2-small-a has far more universal neurons (4.16%) than GPT2-medium (1.23%). The authors speculate that neuron universality decreases in larger models, but say this remains open; Pythia-160M matches GPT2-medium, confounding the size reading.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual-neuron universality across seeds may decrease with model size, the opposite direction to V1's scale trend, but at the neuron level rather than the representation level.

record.problems: The study uses only a narrow range of model families and sizes and compares models trained from different seeds under otherwise shared architecture and data conditions. It studies neuron-level activation recurrence rather than whole-representation similarity; its universality threshold is acknowledged to lack a principled cutoff. The authors note the expense of larger-scale experiments and state that the relationship between scale and universality remains open.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separate numerical recurrence outcomes relevant to the listed versions were left out. Other sections analyze neuron properties, families, weights, entropy effects, and attention-head effects rather than additional cross-model representation alignment outcomes.

untested.parts: Shared subspaces or features beyond the neuron basis, such as subspace or SAE-dictionary matching. The authors suggest dictionary bases as future work.

Recurrence across different model families, architectures or data, and SAE features; only same-architecture seed replicas are compared. Circuits are examined only as simple neuron-to-head or neuron-to-logit motifs.
Whole-representation alignment as models scale; only neuron universality at two small GPT2 sizes, not tied to capability.
No mapping or stitching between models.
No comparison of similarity metrics or input distributions. Threshold dependence is acknowledged but not quantified.
No representation-level alignment or plateau measured; causes of the alignment are not tested.

missing.what: The depth pattern of prediction and suppression neurons is reported as remarkably consistent across all five GPT2-medium seeds and across five Pythia models (410M-6.9B). This is a recurring functional motif across seeds and sizes; it is not rowed.
An (anti-)entropy neuron pair found in GPT2-medium-a recurs, more dramatically, in GPT2-small-a.

The random-rotation baseline correlation values and the max-correlation distributions per model are shown only in figures. GPT2-medium and Pythia-160M have almost identical distributions, and GPT2-small is an outlier.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T5 to T1: the method is Li et al.'s unit-correlation matching, the V3 original source, applied to transformers. V7 links were removed because neuron-basis match rates do not measure representation alignment; the random-rotation baseline shows the measure is basis-dependent. The authors frame seed variation as the smallest change, giving a rough bound for larger changes.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure similarity between whole-model representations or input-point distances, and does not establish a relationship between model scale, capability, and that kind of alignment.
No vision-language model pairs, paired images and captions, or cross-modal alignment are studied.

Tests neuron activation recurrence across random seeds in GPT2 models and supporting Pythia experiments, not shared subspaces or convergence across different architectures, objectives, data, or training stages.
No mapping between model representations, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping is tested.
Tests recurring individual neurons and their interpretations, not recurrence of SAE features or circuits across different model families.

Uses an activation-correlation measure and random-rotation baseline, but does not compare reasonable similarity metrics, settings such as neighbour counts, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs.
The study finds limited neuron-level recurrence in the tested setting, but does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause it, nor whether alignment plateaus.

rows.subject: GPT2-medium-a
rows.operation_detail: Measured neuron activation correlations against GPT2-medium models b-e over 100 million tokens; counted neurons above the excess-correlation threshold.

conditions.value: 100 million tokens from the Pile test set

rows.measure: Count of neurons with excess correlation greater than 0.5
rows.baseline: Mean maximum correlation for a random rotated layer basis is subtracted to calculate excess correlation.
rows.note: The study says there is no principled threshold for universality; this count uses its chosen threshold.
rows.check: Remove V7. V7 concerns representation alignment and its causes, but a neuron-basis match count is not a representation-alignment measure. 1253/98304 is 1.27%, which does not match the 1.23% the paper gives for GPT2-medium.

rows.subject: GPT2-medium
rows.operation_detail: Reported the proportion of neurons classified as universal across the GPT2-medium seed models.

conditions.value: five GPT2-medium models trained from different random seeds

rows.measure: Percentage of neurons classified as universal
rows.baseline: Random-rotation correlations are used in the excess-correlation measure.
rows.note: The paper separately reports 1253 out of 98304 GPT2-medium-a neurons above the threshold; it does not reconcile that count with this percentage.
rows.check: Remove V7, for the same reason as r1. The 1.23% does not reconcile with 1253/98304 (1.27%).

rows.subject: GPT2-small-a
rows.operation_detail: Measured neuron activation correlations against GPT2-small models b-e and reported the fraction above the excess-correlation threshold.
rows.measure: Percentage of neurons classified as universal
rows.baseline: Random-rotation correlations are used in the excess-correlation measure.
rows.note: The reported proportion is higher than for GPT2-medium and Pythia-160M.
rows.check: Remove V7. The 4.16% is the highest of the three models; the authors treat GPT2-small as an outlier.

rows.subject: Pythia-160m
rows.operation_detail: Measured neuron activation correlations across Pythia models trained from different seeds and reported the fraction above the excess-correlation threshold.

conditions.value: five Pythia models trained from different random seeds

rows.measure: Percentage of neurons classified as universal
rows.baseline: Random-rotation correlations are used in the excess-correlation measure.
rows.note: Reported as consistent with GPT2-medium despite the different model family.
rows.check: Remove V7. The Pythia seed replicas are described only in passing; the subject is Pythia-160m.

rows.subject: GPT2-medium-a
rows.operation_detail: Compared each neuron's maximum correlation across other models with its minimum maximum correlation across those models.
rows.measure: Mean difference between max-max and min-max correlation
rows.note: The authors describe relatively little variation in correlations across the other seed models.
rows.check: This measures how consistent each neuron's best match is across the four other seeds, not a recurrence rate. There is no baseline, but the low value (0.049) shows matching is stable across seeds.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V3 when this statistic is considered alone. The reported 0.049 measures variation in best-match correlation across comparison seeds, not the strength or prevalence of shared features.
source_check.problem: Consistently low correlations can also have a small spread; stability alone does not establish V3 convergence.

rows.subject: GPT2-medium-a
rows.operation_detail: Compared each neuron's maximum correlation across other models with its minimum maximum correlation across those models.

conditions.value: neurons with excess correlation greater than 0.5

rows.measure: Mean difference between max-max and min-max correlation
rows.note: The difference is larger for the subset classified as universal than for all neurons.
rows.check: State should be observed, not partial. A 0.105 spread for universal neurons means they recur consistently across all four other seeds. This bears on V5 (recurrence of specific neurons) more than on V3.

rows.subject: GPT2 models
rows.operation_detail: Measured which layer contained each neuron's most correlated neuron across models.
rows.measure: Fraction of neurons by layer whose most correlated counterpart lies in each layer
rows.value: The authors report significant depth specialization.
rows.note: No numerical value for the layer-pair fractions is stated in the text.
rows.check: Qualitative only: no layer-pair fractions are given in the text (Fig 2c). It shows matched units sit at corresponding depths across seeds.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V3 from this measure alone. The authors report depth specialization in the locations of best-matching neurons; no numerical layer-pair fractions or match-strength criterion are supplied for this result.
source_check.problem: The depth of a best match does not establish that the match is strong or that many features are shared.

relationships.condition: GPT2-small, GPT2-medium and Pythia-160m, five seeds each, neuron activation correlation over 100M Pile tokens
relationships.reason: Few units match one-to-one across seeds (1.2-4.2%, r1-r4), consistent with V3's 'not the same individual units'. Matched units are consistent across seeds and depth-specific (r5, r7).
relationships.display_finding: Only 1.2–4.2% of units matched one-to-one across seeds, with matched units showing consistent, depth-specific correspondence.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: GPT2-small, GPT2-medium and Pythia-160m, five seeds each, neuron activation correlation over 100M Pile tokens
source_check.reason: r1-r4 establish a shared neuron-feature subset across seeds, providing restricted support for convergent learning. Low recurrence alone does not establish shared subspaces or the breadth implied by 'many'; r5 and r7 are auxiliary consistency and depth results.

relationships.condition: Seed replicas within GPT2 and Pythia, under the excess correlation > 0.5 criterion
relationships.reason: A subset of neurons recurs across all seeds with little variation (r6), and the study reports interpretable neuron families among them (r1-r4).
relationships.display_finding: A subset of neurons, including interpretable families, recurred across all seeds with little variation under the excess-correlation threshold of 0.5.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Seed replicas within GPT2 and Pythia, under the excess correlation > 0.5 criterion
source_check.reason: r1-r4 establish recurring neuron subsets, r6 reports consistency across comparison seeds, and Section 4.3 identifies interpretable families within the selected subsets.

relationships.condition: Prevalence of recurring neurons in the tested models
relationships.reason: Only about 1-5% of neurons recur (r1-r4). The rate varies by model (GPT2-small 4.16% vs about 1.2% for the others) and rests on a threshold the authors call unprincipled.
relationships.display_finding: Approximately 1–5% of neurons recurred, including 4.16% in GPT2-small versus about 1.2% in the others, under a threshold the authors called unprincipled.

relation.reason: The study directly measures neuron recurrence across independently initialized models and investigates the recurring neurons' interpretations and functions.

tranche.reason: The study addresses convergent learning with neuron activation matching, but its operational measure is excess correlation after subtracting a random-basis baseline. The supplied recipe identifies a different method/measure, so it does not establish the same-method-and-measure requirement for T1.

source_check.notes: The text independently reports both 1253/98304 and 1.23% for GPT2-medium; these do not reconcile arithmetically. Comparisons are within model families across seeds, and non-neuron bases remain untested.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT2 and Pythia seed comparisons using neuron activation correlation
reader_labels.reason: Only 1.23% of GPT2-medium neurons, 4.16% of GPT2-small neurons, and 1.26% of Pythia-160M neurons pass the study's universality threshold, limiting how broadly recurrence can be claimed (r1-r4).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Tested seed replicas under the study's neuron-correlation criterion
reader_labels.reason: The study detects a nonzero subset of recurring neurons across seeds and reports recurring neuron families (r1-r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Prevalence in the tested GPT2 and Pythia models
reader_labels.reason: The recurring neurons constitute a small fraction of neurons under the study's threshold, rather than evidence that universal neurons are widespread (r1-r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Models trained from different seeds within the studied model families
reader_labels.reason: The measured recurrence is incomplete, with only the reported small fractions exceeding the universality threshold; the study does not test whether shared data or objectives explain the recurrence (r1-r4).
